[NFCT.4.4.2] The width of the key sets the behaviour. **Key = ∅** (every slot
`MUTABLE`) is a singleton — one live fact, latest payload wins. **Key = all
slots** is a relation — asserting a tuple that already exists is a **no-op in
working memory** (LFAC.2.5.1): `out_fact` returns the existing wrapper and
`fact_count` is unchanged; a different tuple is a different fact. The no-op is
a **working-memory discipline, not a recording one** — the assert still
arrived, so the `FactAssert` is written and `DS_EV_FACT_ASSERT` **does** fire
([RFCS.6.7]). The key-subset cases (entity-state, composite key) sit between.
